answer: The anemometer on the wind mast logs every gust, and the mast is inspected once a year so the record can be trusted through the winter storms. A reef gust claimed as logged fails the record: the cups must have spun in the wind at the basalt of the storm, and a gust never logged has no speed to quote. Buying a false wind record costs 8,600 in bribes to the inspector and a forged mast, while the violet record is compared with the neighbouring masts, so a gust whose log was never written blows away unrecorded.
